result.finding: Assessed 5 CWE rules in Credentials & Secrets: 4 FOUND, 1 NOT_FOUND
evidence: Scanned all Java source files, frauddetector.properties, and Dockerfile in the ZavaFraudDetector repository for credentials and secrets patterns

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Password
values.description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.

evidence.explanation: frauddetector.properties (committed to source control and bundled into the deployable WAR under WEB-INF/classes/) contains db.****** in plain text. FraudConfig.getDbPassword() reads this property as a fallback when the DB_PASSWORD environment variable is not set, meaning the hard-coded password is always present in the classpath and the deployed artifact.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
values.description: The product uses a hard-coded, unchangeable cryptographic key.

values.name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
values.description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.

evidence.explanation: frauddetector.properties containing database credentials (db.user=sa, db.****** is bundled inside the WAR as WEB-INF/classes/frauddetector.properties with no file permission restrictions. The Dockerfile is based on tomcat:9.0-jdk11 and contains no USER directive, so the container runs as root and all files inherit world-readable permissions. Any process in the container can read the credentials file.

values.name: Insufficient Logging
values.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

evidence.explanation: The application contains no logging framework (no SLF4J, Log4j, java.util.logging, or System.out calls). Security-critical events are silently swallowed: (1) SsoSessionService.resolveSessionUser() catches SQLException with 'catch (SQLException ignored)' — authentication failures are never recorded; (2) SsoSessionService.resolveTokenFromAuthGateway() uses 'catch (Exception ignored)' — auth gateway errors are not logged; (3) FraudConfig static initializer uses 'catch (IOException ignored)' — configuration load failures are not logged; (4) all Action classes catch SQL exceptions without logging. An attacker probing for vulnerabilities or a misconfiguration causing auth bypass would leave no trace.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
values.description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.

evidence.explanation: frauddetector.properties committed to source control contains hard-coded database credentials: db.user=sa (the SQL Server system administrator account) and db.****** These credentials are bundled into the WAR artifact at build time and are always available at runtime as fallback values in FraudConfig.getDbUser() and FraudConfig.getDbPassword(), regardless of whether environment variables are set.
